add.title: LGBTQ people in prison
add.summary: Wikipedia overview article (fetched and read in full, 28 Sep 2026). Its international-standards sections show trans-prisoner placement norms elsewhere (Scotland's 2022 inspection standards admitting trans and intersex prisoners to facilities matching lived/experienced gender; Canada placing by gender identity), but its Brazil paragraph contains no placement rule - only that traumatic social vulnerability and stigma for travestis and transgender people shape rehabilitation. Negative evidence: this general overview reports no codified Brazil-specific trans-prisoner housing policy.

add.title: LGBT rights in Brazil
add.summary: Wikipedia's 'LGBT rights in Brazil' (fetched and read in full, 28 Sep 2026) states, in its Politics section, that LGBTQ people have a special place in Brazilian prisons, separate from other prisoners; that transgender people ('transsexuals') have the right to be called by their social name and not their birth name and to be forwarded to women's prisons; and that LGBTQ prisoners may choose male or female clothing. The statement is footnoted (ref. 253) to a Mix Brasil (UOL) article, 'Vivemos uma inercia no congresso...', archived 18 Jan 2012 - i.e. c.2012-era support for placement-follows-identity in Brazil; treat as dated evidence, recency not re-verified.
